vh-5-1-1-2.title: The Ledger Clerk's Mistake
vh-5-1-1-2.text:
Heavy fog presses against your temples while a clerk from the Cable Court taps a dry knuckle against your leather cradle, muttering about unpaid toll-tariffs. Because your ledger-mark remains unredressed from the upper gates, he assumes you carry company freight, shoves a dry, salted biscuit into your cold palm, and points an ink-stained finger toward an untracked gap in the hawthorn hedge. The bronze tongue hums faintly against your shoulder blades as you weigh whether to slip through the thorny breach or stand your ground.

The damp air smells of wet wool and stale ledger ink.
exits: Squeeze through the narrow hedge gap
Scramble up the slippery apple-wood bank
Tug the dangling bell-pull in the pear grove

vh-5-1-1-3.title: Shivering Beneath the Willow
vh-5-1-1-3.text:
Freezing moisture drips from trailing willow branches down the back of your woollen collar as you pause to readjust the heavy bronze tongue. The bitter mountain wind slips through the valley orchards, threatening to stiffen your leather shoulder straps before you reach the lower terraces. You shift the dead weight of Orison's heart, feeling the cold bronze bite through the padding against your spine.

The grey light fades slightly into the thick mist as you ready your boots for the descent.
exits: Climb over the heap of pruned apple wood
Pick your way past the shattered greenhouse glass
Follow the stampede of sheep into the fog
Tread carefully near the slippery clay dip

vh-5-1-1-4.title: The Blocked Lane
vh-5-1-1-4.text:
An overturned wicker handcart blocks the sunken mud lane, forcing you to turn aside and force a path through a dense patch of stinging nettles. Your thick trousers offer some defense against the bite, but the sudden detour throws off your balance under the heavy cradle. You adjust your footing in the cold slush, listening to the muffled dripping of moisture from the fruit boughs overhead.

The grey murk closes in behind you like a damp wall.
exits: Dodge the falling tile from the shed roof
Step past the buried iron hoops in the humus
Trail your fingers along the damp retaining wall

vh-5-1-1-5.title: Disturbed Pigeons
vh-5-1-1-5.text:
A sudden flurry of wood-pigeons clatters upward into the grey murk, their frantic wings warning of some unseen disturbance lurking deeper in the misty orchard rows. You freeze in your tracks, bracing your knees against the downward pull of the heavy bronze Clapper. The silence that follows their departure feels heavy and deliberate, broken only by the steady dripping of condensation from pear leaves.

You grip the cradle harness tighter and wait for the fog to shift.
exits: Move forward along the damp retaining wall
Walk past the button-eyed scarecrow in the fog
Tighten your grip against the soaked shoulder straps

vh-5-1-2-0.title: The Humming Hives
vh-5-1-2-0.text:
A long row of dormant bee-hives hums with a deep, vibrating resonance that matches the tired ringing deep inside your own marrow. The air here smells faintly of dead wax and frozen honey, thick enough to taste on the back of your tongue. You stand motionless for a moment, letting the shared tremor ease the ache in your shoulders before deciding your next step through the grey veil.

The mist swirls silently around the straw skeps.
exits: Rest your aching back on the old stone bench
Push through the tangle of wild blackberry canes
Turn back toward the guiding stone cistern

vh-5-1-2-1.title: Graves of the Keepers
vh-5-1-2-1.text:
Tilted gravestones of ancient orchard-keepers loom upward from the damp turf like broken teeth in a grey gum. Moss has swallowed their carved names, leaving only rough slate markers standing silent witness in the mist. You step carefully between the sunken mounds, keeping your balance steady as the bronze Clapper shifts slightly in its canvas cradle.

The air smells of wet earth and centuries of fallen leaves.
exits: Pause by the lichen-covered stone bench
Navigate the thorny blackberry briars
Trace the edge of the misty pear branches

vh-5-1-2-2.title: The Copper Basin
vh-5-1-2-2.text:
A rusted copper basin catches the steady drip of condensation from an overhanging branch, going plink-plonking in a slow rhythm that matches your stumbling boots. The stagnant air around the basin smells of rotting pulp and iron-rich water. You pause beside the low stone border, wiping moisture from your forehead while the heavy bronze tongue rests against your spine.

The rhythmic dripping echoes softly through the dead orchard.
exits: Avoid the thorny canes by the dry wall
Step closer to the ditch of fermented windfalls

vh-5-1-2-3.title: Tangled Brambles
vh-5-1-2-3.text:
Wild blackberry brambles reach out from the shadows to snag your leather gaiters and catch upon the cradle harness, threatening to pin you fast in the dripping gloom. You twist your shoulder to shake free of the thorny hooks, feeling the cold weight of the metal shift awkwardly against your back. The mist swirls thicker around your boots as you fight for footing in the mulch.

A single stray thorn scratches sharply through your woollen sleeve.
exits: Ease your load upon the old stone bench
Brush past the snagging blackberry canes
Step over the gurgling iron drainpipe

vh-5-1-2-4.title: The Chipped Note
vh-5-1-2-4.text:
A rogue gust of wind cuts through a gap in the fog, catching the chipped edge of the bronze Clapper and striking a clear, ringing C-natural. The sound startles a roosting pheasant into the grey sky and lays bare a hidden drainage culvert piercing straight through the damp stone wall. Because the metal is bare and damaged, its raw voice carries far in the damp air, revealing a passage you might otherwise have missed.

The vibration dies away into the muffled quiet of the valley.
exits: Follow the path beneath the hanging mist-webs
Cross the narrow alder plank toward the ditch

vh-5-1-2-5.title: The Iron Weir
vh-5-1-2-5.text:
A moss-grown stone weir gurgles beside the muddy track, its icy water tasting strongly of iron and mountain loam. The white noise of the tiny stream drowns out the usual drip of the fog, offering a brief, clear space in the muffled silence. You pause by the low stone barrier to wet your parched throat with the cold mountain runoff before pressing onward.

The current pulls dark and swift beneath its green shroud.
exits: Retrieve the sodden mitten from the track ruts
Cross the rotting alder plank over the ditch
Scatter the fieldfares resting in the hawthorn hedge
